tagline: A legendary hilltop café and Ottoman cemetery above Eyüpsultan — named after the French novelist who came here to write, with the most atmospheric Golden Horn views in Istanbul.

items.name: Pierre Loti Kahvesi
items.description: The hilltop café that has operated on this spot since Pierre Loti himself wrote here in the 1870s. Turkish coffee and tea with unbeatable Golden Horn views.
items.tip: Come at dusk when the Golden Horn turns golden below and the minarets glow. Take the cable car (teleferik) up and walk back down through the Ottoman cemetery.

items.name: Pierre Loti Tepesi
items.description: The hilltop above Eyüpsultan with panoramic views of the Golden Horn waterway, Eyüp's minarets, and the hills beyond. One of Istanbul's most romantic viewpoints.

items.name: Teleferik (Cable Car)
items.description: A short cable car ride from the edge of the Eyüpsultan cemetery to the Pierre Loti hilltop. The ride itself offers excellent views.
items.tip: The cable car runs until late evening. Rides are cheap and the queues are usually minimal outside weekends.

items.name: Tarihi Mezarlık
items.description: The ancient Ottoman cemetery surrounding the cable car route is hauntingly beautiful — centuries-old turbaned marble tombstones among cypress trees.

tips: Pierre Loti is accessed via the Eyüpsultan teleferik (cable car) or a 30-minute walk uphill through the cemetery.
Best visited at sunset or golden hour — the views over the Golden Horn are extraordinary in that light.
Combine with Eyüpsultan Mosque (below) and Fener-Balat (a short bus ride away) for a full Golden Horn day.
A very non-touristy area — you'll mostly see local families and pilgrims here.
